The RM's u0->u1 requires `blocker_moved & has_door_key` simultaneously, but `blocker_moved` is already true at step 1, so the conjunction can only fire if the key is picked up on the very first step — impossible since the key is not at the agent's start cell. When the agent later picks up the key (blocker_moved still true, has_door_key now true), the conjunction `blocker_moved & has_door_key` holds and does fire, since blocker_moved persists as a condition; so the transition is reachable, though the simultaneous reading conflates 'moved' with 'holding'. More seriously, the task's trigger is `blocker_moved` alone: from u0, an episode where the agent idles forever (never picks up the key) violates the property, but the RM never penalizes — there is no timeout/failure state, so episodes that never reach u1 terminate with no negative signal. Also the transition `(u0, door_open) -> u1` skips the key requirement entirely: door_open implies has_door_key causally in the env, so this edge is acceptable as shortcut, but combined with the missing penalty for never acquiring the key, the machine cannot distinguish success from failure of the stated obligation. Predicate-only event usage and else self-loops are fine; FINAL_STATES header present and u2 is the only final state; reward is bounded and dense-ish. To fix: use u0 ->(blocker_moved) u1 requirement state, and add an explicit failure/timeout path or step-limit-aware regression so idle episodes are punished; alternatively make u0's acceptance depend on `has_door_key` occurring after `blocker_moved` via ordering, and reward the final pickup.

The other four predicates match their documented expressions, but the whole set is rejected because of blocker_moved.
